attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated as his observation.

semantics.note: Firm past-tense observation. 'Today' maps to the post date, 2026-06-02. 'Closely resembling' is a fair rendering of 'very much along on these lines' and does not claim the order is identical to his proposal.

contract.note: The plain reading (government checks before release of consequential models, voluntary allowed but noted as a qualification) is an ordinary reading. It neither demands FDA-style mandatory approval nor waters down the claim. The result depends on accepting voluntary pre-release review as 'along these lines'.

evidence.note: Contemporary Roll Call report: the order was signed Tuesday morning, June 2, and requires agencies to build a framework for submitting frontier models up to 30 days before release. It also notes participation is voluntary.

AP report confirms the Tuesday signing and a framework for federal vetting of advanced AI before public release. Voluntary participation and the national-security focus qualify the FDA analogy but do not defeat the contract's support condition.

reviews.rationale: Two independent contemporary reports confirm Trump signed an AI executive order on June 2, 2026 (a Tuesday). It sets up federal review of frontier models up to 30 days before release. That meets the support condition. Participation is voluntary and the focus is national security, so this is not FDA-style approval. But Marcus claimed only similarity, and the contract allows voluntary pre-release review to qualify.
